title: Set a pair of forearm crutches to the same marked hole, each leg's spring button fully out through it
instruction: Set both crutches to the hole ringed in red: each leg's spring button must stand fully out through that hole. Then let go of the crutches.
context: Most people have set a crutch, cane or walker's height, or watched it done after a sprain: press the leg's spring button flush, slide the leg, and let the button spring out through the chosen hole. Instructions from makers and loan services stress that both crutches go in the same hole and every button is fully out: a button caught on the hole's edge lets the leg slip under load.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left, z up from the table); the layout is the same every trial. (1) A fixed pine stand: for each crutch two cradles (a 4 x 2 cm block with a 1 cm post either side of the tube), at y 1 under the collar and y 47 under the tube above the handgrip, and an open pocket 3.4 x 3.4 cm, 7.5 tall, that the handgrip hangs in. (2) Two adult aluminium forearm crutches without locking collars, 0.54 kg each, lying along y on the stand, axes 13.5 above the table at x 23 (near) and 35 (far), tips to the right, cuffs to the left, handgrips hanging straight down, so their backs face up. Each: a main tube 22.2 mm (7/8 in) across, 1.2 mm wall, from a black plastic collar at y 0 up to the cuff (y 55.5 to 61.5, open grey plastic for a 9 cm forearm); a black foam handgrip 3 cm across and 11.5 long at y 36; in the tube's back nine 7 mm holes 1 in apart, hole 1 (lowest, longest setting) at y 4 to hole 9 at y 24.3, with two red tape bands round the tube either side of hole 5 (y 14.2); inside it a 19 mm (3/4 in) leg tube, 58 long, with a black rubber tip 4 across and a chromed steel spring button 6.4 mm across 3 cm below its top end (flat top, edge bevelled 45 degrees), standing 4 mm out of its hole when let out (3 N, 5 N pressed). Handle height (tip to handgrip) is 70 cm at hole 9 to 90.5 at hole 1. The near crutch's button starts in hole 2 (88 cm), the far one's in hole 8 (72.7 cm).
scoring: Judged at the end. A crutch is set when its button stands fully out through the red-banded hole: its middle within 1.5 mm of the hole's middle along the tube and its top at least 3 mm out of the tube (4 mm fully out; caught on the hole's edge or pressed in under the wall, it is not). 0.4 for each crutch set; 1.0 with both set, both let go (every gripper fingertip centre at least 4 cm from both crutches' axes, tip to cuff), and both still on the stand (axis within 1 cm of its height, handgrip within 20 degrees of straight down, slid at most 2 cm along it, not moving). 0 if a crutch was ever dropped (axis 4 cm down or turned over 60 degrees). Possible scores: 0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.0. Real trial: a caliper's depth rod on each button's height and a photo of both red holes. The trial ends at the run limit, or once 1.0 has held 1 s.
reset_notes: Press each button and slide the near crutch's leg back to hole 2 and the far one's to hole 8, buttons fully out; lay both back on the stand, handgrips down. Nothing is used up.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (Isaac Sim, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Tubes, holes and button are modelled at full size and the button is pressed physically (sprung joint, 500 N/m), but its catch is set by the task file: the leg is held at a hole until the button is pressed 3 of its 4 mm, and between holes the button is held in, as the wall does. The leg slides on a joint and can't turn. The tube above the handgrip is straight (real ones bend about 15 degrees). Masses and button force are estimates.
